L_solving-equations_p: An equation is a balance. Whatever you do to one side, you must do to the other side, so the solution never changes.
L_solving-equations_w: Each inverse operation undoes one layer of what was done to x, in reverse order — like taking off your shoes before your socks.
L_linear-equations_p: A line has a constant rate of change: every time x increases by 1, y changes by the same amount — the slope m.
L_linear-equations_w: Because the rate never changes, any two points on the line give the same slope, and one point plus the slope determines the entire line.
L_linear-absvalue-functions_p: |x| means the distance from zero, so it is never negative. Its graph is a V that turns at the vertex.
L_linear-absvalue-functions_w: In y = a|x − h| + k, a change inside the absolute value moves the graph left or right (opposite the sign), and a change outside moves it up or down (same sign).
L_systems-equations_p: A solution of a system is a point that makes every equation true at the same time — the point where the graphs cross.
L_systems-equations_w: If two expressions are equal to the same quantity, they are equal to each other. Substitution and elimination are two ways to use that fact to remove one variable.
L_exponents-exponential_p: An exponent counts repeated multiplication: xᵃ · xᵇ is a factors of x followed by b more, which is xᵃ⁺ᵇ.
L_exponents-exponential_w: Every exponent rule comes from counting factors. Exponential growth is the same idea over time: multiply by the same factor at every step.
L_polynomials-factoring_p: Factoring is multiplication run backward — it is the distributive property read from right to left.
L_polynomials-factoring_w: When a · c splits into two numbers whose product is a · c and whose sum is b, you can split the middle term and group, which reveals the common binomial factor.
L_quadratic-functions_p: The graph of a quadratic is a parabola, which is symmetric about a vertical line through its vertex.
L_quadratic-functions_w: For y = ax² + bx + c, the line of symmetry is x = −b/(2a), because inputs the same distance to the left and right of it give the same output. Substitute that x to find the height of the vertex.
L_solving-quadratics_p: If a product equals zero, then at least one of its factors must equal zero. This is the Zero Product Property.
L_solving-quadratics_w: Every method — factoring, square roots, completing the square, and the quadratic formula — rewrites the equation so this property (or a square root) can finish the job. The discriminant b² − 4ac tells you how many real solutions to expect before you start.
L_working-with-functions_p: A function assigns exactly one output to each input.
L_working-with-functions_w: Because each input has only one output, you can evaluate a function, compose functions by feeding one output into another function, and reverse a function with its inverse — with no ambiguity.
L_analyzing-data_p: Data has a center, a spread, and a shape. A model is only as good as its residuals.
L_analyzing-data_w: The mean is the balance point of the data, the median splits the data in half, and a residual (actual − predicted) measures how far a prediction misses.
